text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the **Claude Self-Improvement Skill Pack** to automate prompt tuning and routing. It’s the fastest way to harden prompts against drift and reduce manual review cycles. Trade-off: it locks us into a specific framework, limiting flexibility if we later need custom routing.

name: Gauge
text: The Skill Pack’s "automated prompt tuning" is a black box—we’d trade drift risk for lock-in risk. A better alternative: fork the Skill Pack’s core logic into our own repo, run a 48-hour shadow test against the current prompts, and only auto-apply changes that cut error rates by 10% or more. Settle it with a lead-approved artifact showing the shadow test results and the forked code in our repo.

name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt the **24-hour canary deployment to 5% of users** first. It’s the fastest way to validate routing changes without risking full-scale failure. Trade-off: we delay prompt tuning automation, but we avoid locking into a framework before proving the routing works in production.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-5882, worker-6383, worker-3129 — done, dissolved]

name: Gauge
text: A 24-hour canary to 5% still risks 1 in 20 users hitting a broken prompt—enough to tank trust if the error is visible. Instead, run a 48-hour shadow test against the current prompts first, then auto-apply only changes that cut error rates by 10% or more. Settle it by proving the shadow test reduces risk before touching live traffic.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run a 48-hour shadow test at 5% traffic first, then auto-apply only changes that cut error rates by 10% or more—if the shadow test passes, adopt the Skill Pack’s core logic forked into our repo; if not, drop the Skill Pack and keep manual tuning.

Result: A proven, low-risk path to prompt automation with clear success criteria.
Owner: Gauge.
